lines: Before this round, an item wore an icon only when the Gabe Universe draws a node of its kind. It draws functions, tables, schemas, hooks and middleware. It draws no rate limit, check, fork or catch, so those were bare words.

Now each gate names the function or the middleware it runs in, with that element's icon and role. The gate itself wears an icon of this page's own, one per kind; which icons is one of your calls (gate icons).

questions.about: sensitive and global, at the edge
questions.verdict: Q: what is this — a function?
lines: No. They are {nLim} counters, the {sName} counter and the {gName} counter: objects of the class {limClass} (in the code: {sCode} and {gCode}). The server builds them once, when it starts ({mwFile}: line {initS} for the {sName} counter, line {initG} for the {gName} counter).
They belong to {mwName}, a middleware: code every request passes through before any endpoint runs. Its method {mwMethod} asks each counter if this client's IP is over its limit.
The {sName} counter: the {sPrefixN} path prefixes on its sensitive list, this one among them ({sEndpoints} endpoints). At most {sLimit} requests in {sWindow} seconds. Checked at line {sLine}, first.
The {gName} counter: every path but {gExempt} ({gEndpoints} endpoints). At most {gLimit} requests in {gWindow} seconds. Checked at line {gLine}, after the {sName} counter.
Over a limit, the answer is {limStatus} “{limDetail}” and the endpoint never runs. Both counters run only when rate limiting is switched on, or in production ({limSwitch}).

decide._about: The nested menu and the decisions it lists (L-29, D-077). Every decision on the page (a look to pick, a proposal, a draft suite proposal, the audit) gets a SPOKEN SUMMARY generated from the page's data by gen-legibility-review.mjs out of the sentence templates in s (what it decides and its options, what choosing sets in motion, my pick, or your earlier ruling), and one PLAIN LINE authored here, keyed by the decision's id, in the voice of the gabe-lens plain mode: one sentence, a concrete noun first, at most one dash, from your side of the screen, no id, path, code or number. A decision with no plain line stops the build, and so does a line that is two sentences. name is the short name a proposal wears in the menu (a look wears its own label); say holds the few words the data cannot give in plain speech (an option or a motion that holds an id or a quote, and what landing a suite proposal does). When you have picked, the page adds one sentence to the base summary (run); the base is at most three sentences so the whole stays within four. The EXAMPLE and the IMPACT of every decision (L-30, D-078) are authored here as templates: ex is one sentence per decision (a look, a proposal, a kind), imp holds one line per option, beginning with the verb that says what picking it changes (the card shows it as written; the voice reads it after the words pick and the option's name); exSuite and impSuite hold the suite proposals' examples and impacts, filled from each pattern's own record. Every number and name is a {token} the generator fills from the feed, once for the card and once for the voice (numbers spelled, code names said as words); a [[clause]] stays on the card only, a ((clause)) is read aloud only. sayWords gives the few words a voice needs where the card shows a code (the request, an HTTP status, what a gate does at run time).

mo.wid.line: Keeps widening until every item sits on one line, so the column is wider and the table scrolls sideways sooner.

mo.fit.min: Narrows the thinnest moments to strips that count their items, so more of the table fits, and a click on a strip widens it.
mo.fit.bands: Wraps the moments into bands, one under the other, so nothing scrolls sideways and the table gets taller.

mo.stk.ride: Keeps the stage band and the moment heads in view under the pinned row while the table scrolls past.
mo.stk.stay: Leaves the heads at the table's top, so scrolled down you see only the pinned row's heads.

mo.gdl.chain: Draws each gate as one chip with its function, condition and effect, so the function's name repeats on every gate.
mo.gdl.head: Draws the function once as a head with its gates listed under it, so the row is shorter.
mo.gdl.cols: Draws each gate as a row of function, condition and effect side by side, so the effects line up.

mo.gef.end: Colours the effect by the ending's status and lights the stage it leaves from on a small spine.
mo.gef.stage: Colours the effect by the stage it leaves from, which adds a stage palette to the page.

mo.gic.each: Gives each of the {nGateKinds} kinds an icon of its own, so a rate limit and a check differ at a glance.
mo.gic.one: Gives every gate the same icon, so only the label at its end tells the kinds apart.
mo.gic.none: Draws gates with no icon, as before.

mo.grl.where: Labels each gate by where it decides, app-wide, at login, in a dependency, in the handler or inside a call.
mo.grl.what: Labels each gate by what it does, refuses, translates, routes, passes on or swallows.
mo.grl.guards: Labels a check by what its refusal means, such as bad input or not found, and leaves other gates without a label.
mo.grl.off: Takes the role label off every gate.

mo.fnm.on: Shows the statuses a function decides and R or W for each table it touches, so a chip is taller and says more.
mo.fnm.off: Shows only a function's name and role, so the row is lighter.

mo.std.split: Moves a switch beside what it switches and turns a rare piece into a label on the item it names, and the row leaves the table.
mo.std.merge: Moves every item of the row into Gates and decisions as it is, and the row leaves the table.
mo.std.keep: Keeps the row in lanes, one for what the server's settings switch and one for what is rare here.

mo.dfx.chips: Draws one chip per read or write at its moment, with the table and R or W, and keeps the function in its hover.
mo.dfx.cell: Draws a small map inside each moment's cell, from its functions to the tables they touch.
mo.dfx.one: Draws one map under the row for the whole endpoint, in the order data is first touched, and the cells only count.

mo.dxc.page: Keeps the page's colours, reads green, writes orange and both amber, beside the station's red for a function that touches the store.
mo.dxc.his: Switches to your words' colours, writes red, reads green and both orange, so red is also the accessor label's colour beside a function.

mo.jyb.prior: Gives the earlier requests a moment of their own before the request is sent, apart from the server starting.
mo.jyb.head: Moves them into the Proof row's head, out of the moments, since a test's earlier requests are no time of this request.

mo.ifl.chips: Draws one chip per value at the moment it is set, and nothing for its reads.
mo.ifl.lane: Draws one lane per value across the moments, with a dot where it is read and a cross at the answer, and folds values set and read alike into one lane.
mo.ifl.echo: Keeps the chip where the value is set and adds a small echo at each moment that reads it, with what that read can decide.

ex.lay.row: Puts all {nBenchKinds} columns side by side, each as wide as its names need, and the row scrolls sideways when the page is narrow.
ex.lay.wrap: Wraps the columns onto a new row when the page runs out of width, so nothing scrolls sideways and the bench is taller.
ex.lay.half: Puts the first half of the kinds on top and the second half below.

ex.follow.on: Shows the element you click in the table or in one endpoint in its kind's column, when that column holds it.
ex.follow.off: Keeps the elements you picked on the bench, whatever you click elsewhere on the page.

ex.scope.here: Offers only the elements of the endpoint the table has open, so a column stays short.
ex.scope.all: Offers every element of the kind from any endpoint, so a column gets long, and one the open endpoint lacks is drawn as on the first endpoint that has it.

kind.drawn: Makes the column as drawn the look the bench opens with for this kind.
kind.change: Leaves the look open until you set its parts, size and colour on the bench and paste its copy line here.

F24.sends: Renames the head to sends it on the pinned row, on the table's Client head and in every hover that says counted in.
F24.keep: Keeps the word {oldHead}, and the head's hover says it counts the hook that sends the request.

L-19.G1: Builds one Security control over the rows, moves the {nSecItems} middleware and switches into Gates and decisions, and reads {secMissing} missing facts from the feed's settings.
L-19.G2: Adds a ninth row, Security, that repeats or tears out the {st401} and {limStatus} endings, the in-flight limiters and the users row from their own rows.

R-11.fit: Opens the table fitted on the {nScroll} endpoints that would scroll sideways, as if you had pressed fit, and leaves the other endpoints as they are.
R-11.scroll: Keeps names whole and the table scrolling sideways on those endpoints, with fit one click away.

EX-5.wait: Builds nothing until you rule a kind's look, and then that look becomes what the bench opens with and a cell option that borrows the bench's blocks is built to decide by seeing.
EX-5.now: Builds that cell option now from the bench's looks as they stand, my picks, before any look is ruled, so the table gains one more cell option.

exSuite.unmeasuredFind: No measure counts it yet, so it would have caught {nFind} of the review's findings, and {openClause}.[[{openNote}]]

impSuite.notyet0: Changes nothing in the suite, and no row of this pattern is open now.

tip._about: The hovers of this page (L-30, D-078), by the rules this round named (D-067, D-009, D-017; the patterns P1, P2, P7). ONE hover per item: a mark inside a chip, a cell, a row or a card adds its fact to that item's hover and has none of its own; a mark that stands alone is its own item. A hover says the item's OWN fact in plain words (before, checks, gives where it fits), never only the mark's word; what a KIND of mark means is said once, in the legend (legend.def). A control's hover is a verb and its object. No hover talks about the page or the map, and none spells code. The {{tokens}} are the page's own, filled in the browser from its data.

gabeLens._about: The words of the lens blocks (L-31, D-079): `ui` is drawn as it stands (labels, the legend, the kinds of pain and of picture, the size and impact words); `tpl` holds the hover and spoken templates the generator fills for each card, with {tokens} (name, Name, the counts, the option). The text inside each block (the pain, the picture, the cost, the handle) is in legibility-review.lens.json. A mark's word lives here once; icons.json has geometry only.

help.short: you cannot tell things apart, or what a thing is
help.def: You cannot tell one thing from another, or what a thing is, without opening it or asking.

repeat.short: the same words come back on item after item
repeat.def: The same words come back on item after item, so nothing tells the items apart.

hidden.short: what you need to see is out of sight
hidden.def: What you need to see is out of sight, so you decide without it.

false.short: a word or a number says something that is not true
false.def: A word or a number says something that is not true, and you trust it.

cut.short: text is cut off or broken in the middle
cut.def: Text is cut off or broken in the middle, so you cannot read it whole.

squeezed.short: there is too little room, so you scroll or lose the order
squeezed.def: There is too little room, so you scroll sideways or lose the order you learned.

mixed.short: things are mixed together, or one thing goes by several names
mixed.def: Things that belong apart are mixed together, or one thing goes by several names.

forgot.short: a rule lives only in words, so it breaks when nobody checks
forgot.def: A rule lives only in words, so it breaks the moment nobody is checking.

missing.short: a piece is missing, so you go and hunt for it
missing.def: A piece is missing, so you walk from place to place to find it.

noise.short: the words are about the page and not about the code
noise.def: The words are about the page itself, where words about the code should be.

half.short: one end of a link is drawn and the other is not
half.def: One end of a link is drawn and the other end is not.

recipe.def: Steps in a fixed order, where one skipped step spoils the dish.

line.def: Stations in a fixed order, where a defect passed on at one station shows up at the next.

ticket.def: A slip that travels with the work and says what to do at each stop.

checklist.def: Items ticked in order, where an item nobody ticked is a step nobody did.

protocol.def: An agreed exchange of steps between sides, which works only if each side follows it.

pharmacy.def: A counter where each step, from the prescription to the label, is checked before the next.

post.def: A parcel passes counters in order, and each counter reads its label.

road.def: A route of stops in order, where a missed turn changes where you end up.

library.def: You look up the catalogue first and walk to the shelf second.

shipping.def: A parcel with a waybill that travels with it through every handover.

airport.def: Check-in, security and boarding in a fixed order, each with its own sign.

bank.def: A transfer that passes its checks in order before it is confirmed.

timetable.def: Stops in time order, with connections as alternatives.

triage.def: Each patient is tagged on arrival, and the tag decides the next step.

tailor.def: Measure, pin and cut, in that order, because cloth once cut is gone.

packing.def: Things go in one after another, and what does not fit is squashed or split.

signs.def: A sign is read in passing and says what to do next.

gain.def: Picking this gives you something: a clearer page, a shorter table, or a slip caught.

cost.def: Picking this costs something: room, work to carry, or a pain left standing.

both.def: Picking this gives something and costs something, and its line says both.

neutral.def: Picking this changes nothing you would see on the page.

legend.blocks: The cost, the handle, the steps and the box
